candidate.label: External foot lever over intact USB mouse
candidate.rationale: Preferred software-first architecture. A separate stable pedal frame routes foot load to its base; a replaceable, compliant tip depresses the original left button. The intact USB electronics remain unmodified. Manufacturer documentation is only an exemplar, not proof of a specimen, force, travel, geometry or descriptor. The eventual host adapter maps normalized donor events to symbolic actions; no real device mapping is implied.

mechanical.load_path: Concept: a separate non-slip base and hinge take the user's foot load; an adjustable compliant contact pushes only the original left-button actuator. Preserve the mouse shell/USB cable and include strain relief. Load capacity and actual specimen geometry are unknown.
mechanical.independent_return: Concept: a separate spring or elastic return lifts the pedal irrespective of mouse-switch spring; verify return reliability with an actual unpowered specimen before any use.
mechanical.travel_stop: Concept: a mechanical stop independent of the original mouse button prevents overtravel; travel gap, button force, max displacement and stop position require physical observation and validation before fabrication.

candidate.label: Conditional remote foot-contact using reclaimed mouse board
candidate.rationale: Second architecture only, not preferred absent teardown. A detached foot switch could actuate the original left-click function while reusing the donor USB controller, but opening the case and identifying the switch contact topology add electrical and mechanical uncertainties. Neither manufacturer product dimensions nor generic HID documentation establish board nodes or safe rewiring. The software-only event adapter can still be checked, but no wiring plan is authorized.

mechanical.load_path: Concept only: a remote foot-switch enclosure carries all user foot load independently of the USB mouse board and reclaimed switch contacts. No actual donor board has been opened or identified.
mechanical.independent_return: Concept only: select a normally released switch mechanism with positive independent return; operating force, actuation count, and donor compatibility are untested.
mechanical.travel_stop: Concept only: remote housing includes its own mechanical travel limit; no measured switch stroke, contact rating, connector, wire gauge or dimensions are supplied.

event.need: Before treating the software adapter as compatible with a real donor, a person must identify the actual salvaged USB mouse, retain its model and condition, and obtain a consented host enumeration/descriptor and observed left-button event mapping. The Logitech B100 document packet is only a product exemplar. Do not infer actual vendor/product IDs, report layout, endpoint, cable condition, or any electrical identity. No live device was connected in this software trial.

Before any pedal CAD, construction or use: obtain nonpowered specimen-specific measurements/assessment of original button actuation force, stroke, case support, clearances, cable strain relief, frame stability and stop position. Confirm a separate pedal return mechanism prevents sustained clicking and that the mechanism cannot overtravel or overload the mouse. These are requested facts, not observations or numeric ranges. Physical approval remains human-controlled; none is granted by software replays.
